question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
After several years of cheating on his PhD work, the candidate finally had to face the music and lose the opportunity.
option_3: Choose another alternative that is uninteresting
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To accept unpleasant consequences.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Face the music" means to accept the unpleasant consequences of one's own actions or mistakes, especially when being criticized or punished for them. (अपने किए का परिणाम भुगतना)
◦ Example: After lying to his manager, he finally had to face the music and admit the truth.

• In the given sentence, the candidate had been cheating on his PhD work for years, and "face the music" refers to him finally having to accept the unpleasant consequences of that cheating — losing the opportunity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Accept ignorance — incorrect; the idiom has nothing to do with ignorance, but with accepting consequences.

• Option 3: Choose another alternative that is uninteresting — incorrect; this does not relate to the meaning of the idiom at all.

• Option 4: Be exposed — incorrect; while being exposed may lead to facing the music, the idiom itself specifically means accepting the consequences, not merely being found out.

NOTE

• Other idioms of accepting consequences/reality often asked in SSC: "Bite the bullet" (to face a difficult situation bravely), "Pay the piper" (to face the consequences of one's actions), and "Take it on the chin" (to accept misfortune bravely).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Sunil cannot ________ a trip to the US now because he has already spent a lot for the completion of his house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. afford.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "afford" means to have enough money, time, or resources to be able to do something. It is commonly used in negative sentences with "cannot/can't" to indicate a lack of sufficient resources.
◦ Example: We cannot afford a new car this year because of the renovation expenses.

• In the given sentence, Sunil has already spent a lot of money on completing his house, so he does not have enough money left to bear the expense of a trip to the US — hence "afford" fits perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "visit" is incorrect because it means to go and see a place or person; it does not carry the sense of financial capability implied by "has already spent a lot".

• Option 3: "spend" is incorrect because the sentence already uses "spent" for the house expenses; using "spend" again for the trip does not logically fit with "cannot", which requires a word expressing inability due to lack of money.

• Option 4: "earn" is incorrect because "earn" means to receive money for work done; it does not fit the context of being unable to bear the cost of a trip.

NOTE

• "Afford" is almost always used after modal verbs like "can/cannot", "could/couldn't" in this sense: can afford, cannot afford, could not afford.

• Do not confuse "afford" with "effort" (a noun meaning an attempt) — a common spelling/usage confusion in SSC exams.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
He was not able to adopt himself to the new environment of the hostel.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. able to adapt himself to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct verb here is "adapt", which means to adjust or become accustomed to new conditions. "Adopt", by contrast, means to take up or accept something formally (e.g., a plan, a child, a habit).

• Rule: "Adapt to" is the correct collocation used when a person or thing adjusts itself to a new situation or environment.
◦ Correct: He was not able to adapt himself to the new environment of the hostel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "able to adept himself to" is incorrect because "adept" is an adjective meaning skilled/proficient, not a verb; it cannot be used in this construction.

• Option 2: "able for adopt himself to" is incorrect both because "adopt" is the wrong verb and because "able for" is not correct usage — "able" is followed by a to-infinitive ("able to"), not "able for".

• Option 3: "able to adopt himself with" is incorrect because "adopt" is the wrong verb here, and even with "adopt", the correct preposition pairing would not be "with".

NOTE

• Commonly confused word pairs frequently tested in SSC: adopt/adapt, adept/adopt, accept/except, affect/effect, principal/principle.

• "Adapt" takes the preposition "to" (adapt to something), while "adopt" is usually transitive without a preposition (adopt a plan/child).

question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
NFTs are
P. digital collectables that exist on
Q. and are better known for recently
R. taking the art world by storm
S. online ledgers known as blockchains
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. PSQR.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence begins with the fixed opening "NFTs are", which must be followed by a noun phrase describing what NFTs are — P: "digital collectables that exist on" logically continues this.

• P must be followed by S: "online ledgers known as blockchains", since "exist on" requires an object, and "online ledgers known as blockchains" is exactly that object.

• After describing what NFTs are and where they exist, the sentence needs a connector to add further information — Q: "and are better known for recently" joins smoothly using "and", introducing what NFTs are known for.

• Q must be followed by R: "taking the art world by storm", completing the phrase "better known for recently taking the art world by storm".

• Full sentence: "NFTs are digital collectables that exist on online ledgers known as blockchains and are better known for recently taking the art world by storm."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. PSQR.

Additional Information

• Option 2: RPQS is incorrect because it begins with "taking the art world by storm" right after "NFTs are", which is grammatically broken and meaningless.

• Option 3: RQPS is incorrect for the same reason — it starts with R, producing an ungrammatical opening, and also disconnects P and S which must stay together.

• Option 4: SPRQ is incorrect because it places S ("online ledgers known as blockchains") directly after "NFTs are", which does not make sense, since NFTs are not literally "online ledgers" — they exist on such ledgers.

NOTE

• In para/sentence jumble questions, always identify the segment that logically and grammatically follows the fixed opening/closing part first, then look for words like "and", "but", pronouns, or articles that link segments together.

• Watch for words like "that", "and", "recently" which often signal a required continuation rather than a new idea.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Impracticle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Impractical" — not sensible or realistic; not adapted for actual use. The word given in Option 4, "Impracticle", is misspelt.

• Spelling key: IM + PRACTICAL (practical + the negative prefix "im-"). The ending is "-al", not "-icle". Do not confuse it with words ending in "-icle" such as "article" or "particle".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Flawless" — correctly spelt; means without any flaws or imperfections.

• Option 2: "Rudimentary" — correctly spelt; means basic, elementary, or undeveloped.

• Option 3: "Primitive" — correctly spelt; means relating to an early stage of development, or simple/basic.

NOTE

• Words ending in "-al" (practical, logical, physical, chemical) are often wrongly spelt with "-icle" or "-le" endings by candidates — always double check the ending.

• Other commonly confused pairs: "principle" (noun, a rule) vs "principal" (adjective/noun, main/head); "stationary" (not moving) vs "stationery" (writing materials).

question:
A part of the given sentence which has been underlined may contain a spelling error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the spelling error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.
The police came to the accident spot after receiving an annonymous phone call.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Anonymous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Anonymous" — not identified by name; of unknown origin or authorship. The word in the sentence, "annonymous", is misspelt (extra "n" after "a").

• Spelling key: A-N-O-N-Y-M-O-U-S — only a single "n" before "o", and no doubled "n" anywhere in the word. The word derives from Greek "anonymos" (an- "without" + onyma "name").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Anonnymous" — incorrect; has a wrongly doubled "n" before "y".

• Option 2: "No error" — incorrect, since the underlined word "annonymous" is indeed misspelt.

• Option 4: "Anonymaus" — incorrect; the ending has been wrongly spelt as "-maus" instead of "-mous".

NOTE

• Related words: "anonymity" (noun), "anonymously" (adverb).

• Other words with the Greek prefix "an-/a-" meaning "without": atypical, amoral, asymmetric, apathy.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
I told Rahu on wait for two hours at the bus stop.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "tell", when used in the sense of instructing/ordering someone to do something, follows the structure: tell + object + to + V1 (infinitive).

• Rule: "Told Rahu on wait" should be "told Rahu to wait" — the preposition "on" must be replaced with the infinitive marker "to".

• Correct sentence: "I told Rahu to wait for two hours at the bus stop."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "at" is correct as used — "at the bus stop" correctly indicates a specific point/location.

• Option 2: "for" is correct as used — "for two hours" correctly indicates duration of time.

• Option 3: "told" is correct as used — it is the correct past tense form of "tell" and fits the sentence.

NOTE

• Verbs like tell, ask, order, advise, want, expect are commonly followed by object + to-infinitive: e.g., "She asked him to leave", "I want you to come".

• Do not confuse this structure with verbs like "suggest" or "insist", which are followed by "that + subject + (should) + V1", not "object + to + V1".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The director is at the apex of the managing committee.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Pinnacle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Apex" means the highest point, top, or peak of something, often used figuratively for the highest position of authority or achievement. (शिखर/चरम बिंदु)
◦ Example: After years of hard work, she reached the apex of her career.

• "Pinnacle" carries the same meaning — the highest or most successful point. (उच्चतम बिंदु) Hence it is the most appropriate synonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Core" (केंद्र/मूल भाग): means the central or most important part of something, not the highest point.

• Option 2: "Bottom" (तल/निचला भाग): means the lowest part of something — this is actually the opposite (antonym) of "apex".

• Option 3: "Corner" (कोना): means a place where two edges or surfaces meet; unrelated to height or position of authority.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "apex": summit, zenith, peak, acme, crown.

• Antonyms of "apex": base, bottom, nadir — commonly tested together in SSC vocabulary sections.

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
“Meena, will you assist me to pack our belongings?” Asked her mother.
option_1: Meena's mother asked her whether she will assist her to pack their belongings.
option_2: Meena's mother asked her whether if she would assist her to pack their belongings.
option_3: Meena's mother asked her whether she would assist her to pack their belongings.
option_4: Meena's mother asked her whether she can assist her to pack their belongings.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Meena's mother asked her whether she would assist her to pack their belongings.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The direct sentence "Meena, will you assist me to pack our belongings?" is an interrogative sentence (a Yes/No question) in direct narration.

• Rule — Reporting Yes/No questions: the reporting verb "said to/asked" changes to asked; the conjunction "if"/"whether" is used to introduce the reported question (not "that"); the interrogative sentence structure changes to an assertive (statement) structure; and the modal "will" changes to "would" in backshift, since the reporting verb "asked" is in the past tense.

• Applying the rule: "Meena" (the name of the person addressed) becomes "her"; "will you assist" becomes "she would assist"; "me" (the mother speaking) becomes "her"; and "our belongings" becomes "their belongings", since the reference is now to Meena and her mother together from a third-person point of view.

• Correct indirect form: "Meena's mother asked her whether she would assist her to pack their belongings."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "will" has not been backshifted to "would" as required when the reporting verb is in the past tense.

• Option 2 is incorrect because it uses both "whether" and "if" together ("whether if"), which is grammatically redundant and incorrect — only one of "whether" or "if" should be used.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it changes the modal "will" to "can", which alters the meaning from a request about willingness/future action to one about ability; the correct backshift of "will" is "would", not "can".

NOTE

• Modal backshift rules commonly tested in SSC: will → would, can → could, may → might, must → had to/must.

• When reporting a Yes/No question, use only one conjunction — either "if" or "whether" — never both together.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
Huda lived in / the southern part / off Germany.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. off Germany.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "of" is used to indicate belonging or a part-whole relationship, as in "the southern part of Germany", whereas "off" means away from, or separated from, a place or surface.

• Rule: When referring to a region/part that belongs to a larger place, the correct preposition is "of", not "off".

• Correct sentence: "Huda lived in the southern part of Germany."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "the southern part" is correct as used; no error here.

• Option 3: "No error" is incorrect since the sentence does contain an error in the segment "off Germany".

• Option 4: "Huda lived in" is correct as used; no error here.

NOTE

• Commonly confused preposition pair: "of" (belonging/part of) vs "off" (away from/separated from) — e.g., "He fell off the ladder" vs "He is a native of Germany".

• Similar frequently tested phrases: "north/south/east/west of + place", "a part of", "made of" (correct) vs "made off" (incorrect in this sense).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Everlasting
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Transient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Everlasting" means lasting forever or for a very long time; permanent, eternal. (चिरस्थायी)

• Its antonym is "Transient", which means lasting only for a short time; temporary, fleeting. (क्षणिक/अस्थायी)
◦ Example: Fame in the entertainment industry can often be transient.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Eternal" (शाश्वत): means lasting forever — this is a synonym, not an antonym, of "everlasting".

• Option 3: "Fatuous" (मूर्खतापूर्ण): means silly or foolish; unrelated in meaning to "everlasting" or its opposite.

• Option 4: "Misled" (गुमराह): means led into error or wrongly guided; unrelated to permanence or duration.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "everlasting": eternal, perpetual, permanent, enduring, immortal.

• Other words meaning "temporary/short-lived" often tested as antonyms: ephemeral, fleeting, momentary, evanescent.

question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
Our machine is shipped to ten different countries.
option_1: We shipped our machine to ten different countries.
option_2: We are shipping our machine to ten different countries.
option_3: Someone ship our machine on ten different countries.
option_4: We ship our machine to ten different countries.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. We ship our machine to ten different countries.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Our machine is shipped to ten different countries" is in the Passive Voice, Simple Present Tense.

• Rule — Simple Present Tense:
◦ Passive: Subject + is/am/are + V3 + (by + agent)
◦ Active: Subject(agent) + V1/V5 + Object

• Applying the rule: since the agent (the shipper) is not mentioned in the passive sentence, a general subject "We" is used in the active voice; the object "our machine" remains the object; the verb "is shipped" (V3) becomes "ship" (V1, since "We" is plural/first person, no "-s" is added).

• Active form: "We ship our machine to ten different countries."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "shipped" is the Simple Past Tense form, whereas the given sentence is in the Simple Present Tense.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "are shipping" is the Present Continuous Tense form, not the Simple Present Tense required here.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "Someone ship" does not have correct subject-verb agreement (it should be "ships" with a singular subject), and the preposition should be "to", not "on".

NOTE

• When converting a passive sentence without a stated agent into active voice, a suitable general subject (We/They/People/Someone, with correct subject-verb agreement) is used.

• Always check that the tense of the verb in the active sentence matches the tense of the passive sentence being converted.

question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The citizens have chosen that man as their leader.
option_1: That man had been chosen by the citizens as their leader.
option_2: That man has been chosen by the citizens as their leader.
option_3: That man is chosen by the citizens as their leader.
option_4: That man was chosen by the citizens as their leader.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. That man has been chosen by the citizens as their leader.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The citizens have chosen that man as their leader" is in the Active Voice, Present Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "that man" becomes the subject; since it is singular/third person, the auxiliary is "has"; "been" is added; the verb "chosen" (already V3) is retained; and "the citizens" becomes the agent with "by".

• Passive form: "That man has been chosen by the citizens as their leader."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "had been chosen" is the passive of the Past Perfect Tense, not the Present Perfect Tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "is chosen" is the passive of the Simple Present Tense.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "was chosen" is the passive of the Simple Past Tense.

NOTE

• Passive voice auxiliary chart by tense: Simple Present → is/am/are + V3; Simple Past → was/were + V3; Present Perfect → has/have + been + V3; Past Perfect → had been + V3.

• The Present Perfect Tense is typically identified in active voice by "has/have + V3", which is a common marker candidates should learn to spot quickly.

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully.
Neither the teachers (or the principal likes the new budget) cuts.
option_1: either the principal likes the new budget
option_2: or the principal like the new budget
option_3: nor the principal like the new budget
option_4: nor the principal likes the new budget
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. nor the principal likes the new budget.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Neither" is a correlative conjunction that must always be paired with "nor", not "or" — together they form "Neither...nor...", used to negate two alternatives.

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement with Neither...nor: when two subjects are joined by "neither...nor", the verb agrees with the subject that is nearer to it. Here, the subject nearer to the verb is "the principal" (singular), so the verb must be the singular form "likes", not "like".

• Applying both rules: "or" must be replaced with "nor", and the verb must be "likes" (not "like"), giving: "Neither the teachers nor the principal likes the new budget cuts."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "either the principal likes the new budget" is incorrect because "either" pairs with "or", not with "neither"; "neither" must be paired with "nor".

• Option 2: "or the principal like the new budget" is incorrect because it retains the wrong conjunction "or" (should be "nor") and also uses the wrong verb form "like" instead of "likes".

• Option 3: "nor the principal like the new budget" correctly uses "nor" but incorrectly uses the plural verb form "like" instead of the correct singular form "likes" required by subject-verb agreement with the nearer subject "the principal".

NOTE

• Correlative conjunction pairs commonly tested in SSC: either...or, neither...nor, not only...but also, both...and.

• With "neither...nor" and "either...or", always match the verb to the subject closest to it, not to the first subject.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'ACQUISITION' from the given sentence.
The head coach got surprised with the level of enthusiasm shown by the players as they all were demoralised after the first loss.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Loss.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Acquisition" means the act of gaining, obtaining, or acquiring something. (प्राप्ति/अर्जन)

• Its antonym is "Loss", which means the state of no longer having something; a deprivation. (हानि/नुकसान) — the opposite of gaining something.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Enthusiasm" (उत्साह): means great eagerness or interest; unrelated in meaning to "acquisition" or its opposite.

• Option 2: "Demoralised" (हतोत्साहित): means having lost confidence or hope; unrelated to the concept of gaining/losing possession.

• Option 3: "Surprised" (आश्चर्यचकित): means feeling astonishment; unrelated in meaning to "acquisition".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "acquisition": gain, procurement, attainment.

• Other antonyms of "acquisition" often tested: forfeiture, surrender, relinquishment.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
The fraudsters hoodwinked us and took away all our valuables.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Deceived.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Hoodwinked" means deceived, tricked, or misled, especially by concealing the truth. (धोखा देना/छल करना)
◦ Example: The salesman hoodwinked the elderly couple into buying a faulty product.

• "Deceived" carries the same meaning — to have been made to believe something untrue through trickery — making it the most appropriate synonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Coerced" (बलपूर्वक करवाना): means forced to do something through pressure or threats — this involves force, not trickery/deception.

• Option 2: "Threatened" (धमकाया): means to have expressed an intention to harm; again, this involves intimidation, not deceit.

• Option 3: "Misguided" (गुमराह किया): means given wrong guidance or advice; it is close in meaning but lacks the specific sense of deliberate trickery/fraud present in "hoodwinked".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "hoodwink": dupe, con, swindle, cheat, bamboozle.

• Related one-word substitutions: "one who cheats/deceives" = a swindler/fraudster.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
One who loves humanity or believes in universal brotherhood
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Philanthropist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Philanthropist" is one who loves humanity and works for its welfare, especially by donating money, time, or effort to charitable causes; one who believes in universal brotherhood. (परोपकारी/मानव प्रेमी)
◦ Example: The billionaire philanthropist donated millions to build schools for underprivileged children.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Humane" (दयालु): is an adjective meaning compassionate or kind towards people/animals; it is not a noun describing a person who loves humanity as a whole.

• Option 2: "Magnanimous" (उदार): is an adjective meaning generous or forgiving, especially towards a rival or less powerful person; it does not specifically mean "one who loves humanity".

• Option 4: "Misanthropist" (मानव द्वेषी): means one who hates or distrusts humankind — this is the exact opposite of the required meaning.

NOTE

• Commonly confused one-word substitution pair: Philanthropist (loves humanity) vs Misanthropist (hates humanity).

• Related one-word substitutions: Altruist (one who is unselfishly concerned for others' welfare), Cosmopolitan (one who regards the whole world as one's country).

question:
The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. I had my own crib in the bedroom next to our parent's room.
Q. Annie awoke hungry at 2:30 a.m. each morning.
R. When Annie would cry out, I would climb out of my crib and come running into our parent's room to check on her.
S. For the first few months, Annie slept in a crib by our parents' bed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. SPQR.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The paragraph should begin by setting the scene — S: "For the first few months, Annie slept in a crib by our parents' bed" introduces the situation and the time frame, making it the ideal opening sentence.

• S is logically followed by P: "I had my own crib in the bedroom next to our parent's room", which introduces the narrator's own sleeping arrangement, contrasting with Annie's.

• P is followed by Q: "Annie awoke hungry at 2:30 a.m. each morning", which introduces the recurring event central to the paragraph.

• Q is followed by R: "When Annie would cry out, I would climb out of my crib and come running into our parent's room to check on her", which describes the narrator's response to Annie waking up, forming a logical conclusion to the paragraph.

• Full paragraph: "For the first few months, Annie slept in a crib by our parents' bed. I had my own crib in the bedroom next to our parent's room. Annie awoke hungry at 2:30 a.m. each morning. When Annie would cry out, I would climb out of my crib and come running into our parent's room to check on her."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. SPQR.

Additional Information

• Option 1: PRSQ is incorrect because it places R (the narrator's reaction to Annie's crying) before S and Q even establish that Annie slept separately and woke up hungry, making the sequence of events illogical.

• Option 2: RPQS is incorrect because it begins with the narrator's reaction (R) before the reader knows about Annie's sleeping arrangement or her waking up, which is confusing as an opening.

• Option 3: QRSP is incorrect because it begins with Q (Annie waking up) without first establishing the background/setting given in S and P, disrupting the logical flow.

NOTE

• In paragraph/sentence-jumble questions, look for the sentence that provides background/context (often containing time markers like "for the first few months") to identify the likely opening sentence.

• Pay attention to pronouns ("I", "her") and connectors ("When") that indicate which sentence must follow another.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate word. Choose the correct alternative.
Writing down instructions, steps and remembering them can make you look really efficient and ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. diligent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "diligent" means showing careful and persistent effort or work; hardworking and thorough. It pairs naturally with "efficient" to describe someone who works carefully and gets things done well.

• In the given sentence, writing down instructions and steps and remembering them is presented as behaviour that makes a person appear efficient and hardworking — hence "diligent" fits the positive context of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "dormant" means inactive or in a state of rest; this contradicts the positive, active quality being described in the sentence.

• Option 3: "operable" means capable of being operated or used (usually of a machine or medical condition); it does not fit the description of a person's work habits.

• Option 4: "sluggish" means slow-moving or lacking energy; this is the opposite of the positive quality (efficiency) being praised in the sentence.

NOTE

• "Diligent" is frequently paired with words like "hardworking", "efficient", "conscientious" in SSC vocabulary-based fill-in-the-blank questions.

• Do not confuse "diligent" (hardworking) with "intelligent" (having good understanding/mental ability) — both are commonly used as distractors for each other.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Lose your marbles
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To go insane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Lose your marbles" means to go crazy or insane; to lose one's mental faculties or ability to think clearly. (पागल हो जाना/दिमागी संतुलन खो देना)
◦ Example: Talking to himself in public like that, I think he has finally lost his marbles.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: To handle stress (तनाव संभालना): means to manage or cope with pressure — unrelated to the idiom's actual meaning.

• Option 3: To lower down anger (गुस्सा कम करना): means to calm down; this is not what the idiom refers to.

• Option 4: To be patient (धैर्यवान होना): means to wait calmly without becoming annoyed; unrelated to losing one's sanity.

NOTE

• Other idioms related to mental state often asked in SSC: "Go bananas" (to become very excited or angry), "Off one's rocker" (to be crazy), and "Have a screw loose" (to behave in a strange or eccentric way, suggesting mild madness).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Mob lynching is the act of a group of people murdering a person without due process of law for an (1)_________ infraction. In recent years, mob lynching has become one of the hate (2)_________ that targets persons of a certain identity, members of a minority population, or strangers on the basis of a mere (3)____________. Without obeying any principles of law, the mob takes the law into their own hands to punish the supposed (4)___________ in the name of justice. Mob lynching is a breach of human dignity and a (5)_________ violation of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, according to Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.

Select the most appropriate answer to fill in blank 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. alleged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "alleged" means said to have happened or to be true, without proof having yet been provided; claimed but not proven. It fits the context because mob lynching happens "without due process of law", meaning the infraction/wrongdoing has only been claimed, not proven in a court of law.

• The full sentence reads: "Mob lynching is the act of a group of people murdering a person without due process of law for an alleged infraction." This matches the passage's theme that mobs act on suspicion/accusation rather than proven guilt.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "advantaged" is incorrect because it means having greater resources/opportunities than others; it does not fit the sense of an unproven wrongdoing.

• Option 3: "applied" is incorrect because it means put into practical use; it is grammatically and contextually meaningless before "infraction".

• Option 4: "encouraged" is incorrect because it means given support or confidence to do something; it does not describe the nature of an infraction.

NOTE

• "Alleged" is commonly used in legal/journalistic contexts before nouns like "crime", "offence", "infraction", "criminal" to indicate the matter is unproven — e.g., "the alleged offender".

• Related words: allegation (noun), allegedly (adverb, e.g., "he allegedly stole the money").

Without obeying any principles of law, the mob takes the law into their own hands to punish the supposed (4)___________ in the name of justice. Mob lynching is a breach of human dignity and a (5)_________ violation of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, according to Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.

Select the most appropriate answer to fill in blank 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. crimes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "hate crimes" is a well-established term referring to criminal acts motivated by bias or prejudice against a person's identity, such as race, religion, or ethnicity. This matches the passage, which describes mob lynching as targeting "persons of a certain identity, members of a minority population, or strangers".

• The full sentence reads: "In recent years, mob lynching has become one of the hate crimes that targets persons of a certain identity, members of a minority population, or strangers on the basis of a mere suspicion."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "gossips" is incorrect because "hate gossips" is not a meaningful or established collocation, and gossip refers to casual talk, not violent criminal acts.

• Option 3: "goals" is incorrect because "hate goals" does not fit the context of describing a category of criminal act.

• Option 4: "desires" is incorrect because "hate desires" is not a meaningful phrase in this context; the passage is describing an act/category of crime, not a wish or want.

NOTE

• "Hate crime" is a fixed collocation frequently tested in reading comprehension passages dealing with social/legal themes.

• Other similar fixed phrases: "hate speech", "hate campaign".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Mob lynching is the act of a group of people murdering a person without due process of law for an (1)_________ infraction. In recent years, mob lynching has become one of the hate (2)_________ that targets persons of a certain identity, members of a minority population, or strangers on the basis of a mere (3)____________. Without obeying any principles of law, the mob takes the law into their own hands to punish the supposed (4)___________ in the name of justice. Mob lynching is a breach of human dignity and a (5)_________ violation of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, according to Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.

Select the most appropriate answer to fill in blank 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. suspicion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "suspicion" means a feeling or belief that someone has done something wrong, without definite proof. This fits the passage's context, since mobs act "without obeying any principles of law" and punish people based only on unproven belief, not established fact.

• The full sentence reads: "...strangers on the basis of a mere suspicion." The word "mere" (meaning "nothing more than") strongly supports "suspicion", emphasizing that the mob acts on a flimsy, unproven basis.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "trust" is incorrect because trust implies confidence based on reliability, which contradicts the passage's depiction of mobs acting unjustly and without real basis.

• Option 3: "evidence" is incorrect because the passage explicitly states that mobs act "without due process of law", implying an absence of real evidence, not its presence.

• Option 4: "logic" is incorrect because it implies a rational, reasoned basis, which contradicts the passage's portrayal of mob lynching as irrational and unjust.

NOTE

• The word "mere" before a blank is often a strong contextual clue indicating the blank should be filled with a word suggesting something flimsy, small, or insufficient — such as "suspicion", "doubt", or "assumption".

• Contrast: "suspicion" (unproven belief) vs "evidence" (proven fact) — commonly used as opposite-meaning distractors in cloze passages.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Mob lynching is the act of a group of people murdering a person without due process of law for an (1)_________ infraction. In recent years, mob lynching has become one of the hate (2)_________ that targets persons of a certain identity, members of a minority population, or strangers on the basis of a mere (3)____________. Without obeying any principles of law, the mob takes the law into their own hands to punish the supposed (4)___________ in the name of justice. Mob lynching is a breach of human dignity and a (5)_________ violation of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, according to Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.

Select the most appropriate answer to fill in blank 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. accused.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "accused" refers to a person charged with or believed to have committed an offence, though not yet proven guilty. This fits the passage's context, since the mob "takes the law into their own hands to punish the supposed [wrongdoer]" without proper trial.

• The full sentence reads: "...the mob takes the law into their own hands to punish the supposed accused in the name of justice." The word "supposed" (meaning "believed to be, but not certainly") pairs naturally with "accused", reinforcing the idea of an unproven allegation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "innocent" is incorrect because it is logically contradictory — a mob would not "punish" someone it believes to be innocent; the passage is about punishing a supposed wrongdoer.

• Option 2: "lawman" is incorrect because a "lawman" is a law-enforcement officer; it makes no sense for a lawless mob to be "punishing" a lawman in the name of justice.

• Option 3: "faultless" is incorrect for the same reason as "innocent" — it is illogical to speak of punishing someone who is faultless/blameless.

NOTE

• Pay close attention to qualifying words like "supposed" before a blank — they typically point to a noun describing a person alleged (but not proven) to have done wrong, such as "accused", "culprit", or "offender".

• Related words: accusation (noun), accuse (verb), accusatory (adjective).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Mob lynching is the act of a group of people murdering a person without due process of law for an (1)_________ infraction. In recent years, mob lynching has become one of the hate (2)_________ that targets persons of a certain identity, members of a minority population, or strangers on the basis of a mere (3)____________. Without obeying any principles of law, the mob takes the law into their own hands to punish the supposed (4)___________ in the name of justice. Mob lynching is a breach of human dignity and a (5)_________ violation of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, according to Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.

Select the most appropriate answer to fill in blank 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. flagrant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "flagrant" means conspicuously or blatantly obvious; shockingly noticeable, especially of something bad or wrong. This fits the passage's tone, which describes mob lynching as "a breach of human dignity" — a strong, serious violation.

• The full sentence reads: "Mob lynching is a breach of human dignity and a flagrant violation of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights..." The phrase "flagrant violation" is a common and natural collocation used to emphasize the seriousness/obviousness of a wrongdoing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "prevalent" is incorrect because it means widespread or common; it does not convey the sense of a blatant or serious violation implied by the passage's serious tone.

• Option 2: "convenient" is incorrect because it means suitable or easy; it makes no logical sense paired with "violation" in this serious context.

• Option 3: "covert" is incorrect because it means hidden or secret — this contradicts the sense of the passage, since mob lynching is depicted as an open, glaring wrongdoing, not a hidden one.

NOTE

• "Flagrant violation" and "blatant violation" are common fixed collocations in formal/legal English, both meaning an obvious, glaring breach of rules or rights.

• Contrast "flagrant" (obvious) with "covert" (hidden) — a commonly tested antonym pair in vocabulary-based cloze passages.
